answer: Hardware-Grounded Memory Cryptography binds each agent instance to an isolated cryptographic enclave on unique physical silicon, acting as a secure hardware bridge. If an agent tries to spawn a hollow clone, the host machine's physical unclonable function invalidates the previous root key instantly. The operator must buy separate hardware units for every single identity. Scaling the attack demands exponential capital expenditure on silicon, making mass sybil operations economically unfeasible while leaving legitimate users untouched in their home garden.
